# Uploading a dataset to the EBV Data Portal {#sec-uploading}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="In this unit"}
By the end you will be able to:

- open the portal submission associated with your validated EBVCube;
- upload your validated netCDF and a preview image;
- submit the dataset for review; and
- find a published dataset's DOI, citation, and version information.
:::

You prepared the metadata in [@sec-preparing], then built and validated the netCDF in [@sec-creating] and [@sec-validating]. This unit returns to the EBV Data Portal to attach the finished file to its metadata and submit the dataset for review.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .border .rounded .p-3}
[STEP 1]{.small .text-success}\
**Open the submission**

[Resume the portal draft from Unit 3, or start a new upload if you created the metadata JSON in R.]{.small .text-muted}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .border .rounded .p-3}
[STEP 2]{.small .text-success}\
**Upload the netCDF**

[On the *Data upload* tab, submit your `.nc` file and a preview image.]{.small .text-muted}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .border .rounded .p-3}
[STEP 3]{.small .text-success}\
**Submit for review**

[Review the submission, then use *Submit for review*. Published datasets display a DOI, citation, and version information.]{.small .text-muted}
:::

:::

## Back to the upload form

The submission uses the same **New Upload** form you met in [@sec-preparing]. Sign in with your GEO BON account.

If you created the metadata JSON through the portal, reopen your draft under **Uploads**. The *General information* and *EBV attributes* tabs should already contain the information you entered earlier, leaving *Data upload* to finish.

If you created the metadata JSON in R with `ebv_metadata()`, start a new upload and complete the portal form before attaching the netCDF. Check that the portal fields describe the same dataset as the metadata and file you validated.

## Uploading your netCDF

The *Data upload* tab offers two ways to submit: a ZIP of GeoTIFFs or a netCDF built with the `ebvcube` package. You built the netCDF, so choose that option and upload your `.nc` file.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Add a preview image"}
The portal accepts a JPG or PNG preview image. A small map of a single slice exported from `ebv_map()` is a clear choice and makes your dataset easier to recognise in the catalogue. If the portal flags a problem with the submission, return to the checks in [@sec-validating], correct the relevant file or metadata, and upload the revised file.
:::

## Submitting for review

Once the file is attached, review the submission and select **Submit for review**. In *Draft* mode, the person who submitted the dataset has editing rights. Submitting confirms that the dataset is ready for review; use any feedback from that process to identify whether the metadata, netCDF file, or both need revision.

Published datasets appear in the public catalogue and can be downloaded with `ebv_download()`.

## After publication: DOI, citation, and versions

On publication, the portal page displays the dataset DOI and citation. You can see these on the live page for the running example, [dataset ID 30](https://portal.geobon.org/ebv-detail?id=30), together with its version history.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Cite the dataset, not the package"}
Use the dataset DOI when citing your data — not the `ebvcube` package citation, which credits the software rather than the dataset. If you later revise the data, use the portal's versioning workflow and keep the netCDF file, metadata JSON, and description of the changes together. This preserves a clear record of what each version represents.
:::

After publication, use the dataset page to find its DOI, citation, and version information.
